headline: Investors look longingly to Asia - Taipei Times
summary: Investors are turning to Asia as focus shifts away from the US-Israeli war on Iran. Shares in South Korea and Taiwan have rallied the most globally this month, with the KOSPI up 78 percent.
why: The KOSPI is South Korea's main benchmark index, heavily weighted toward semiconductors, so its moves reflect global chip demand and regional capital flows.

impacts.name: KOSPI
impacts.why: The article states the KOSPI has surged 78 percent, leading regional gains.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Investors shifting attention away from the Iran war have pushed capital into Asian equities, with South Korea and Taiwan leading gains.
